note: The fuzzer-controlled date string enters the real date parser as str; this candidate is a one-byte non-NUL invalid UTF-8 leading byte.
The unchecked parser input is passed to the locale-aware tokenization path without validating that it is complete UTF-8.
The invalid byte is not a digit, so fewer than three numeric tokens are found and the month-name matching path processes the whole input as UTF-8 text.
The code sends the NUL-terminated but UTF-8-invalid input to g_utf8_casefold with len -1; the missing safety obligation is that str must be valid complete UTF-8 before this call.
With len negative, iteration is controlled only by dereferencing p for a NUL byte; after g_utf8_next_char skips according to the malformed leading byte, p can move past the allocated terminator.
For the candidate byte 0xf0, g_utf8_next_char advances p by four bytes even though the heap string contains only the byte and its terminating NUL.
The next loop test dereferences p after it has advanced beyond the two-byte heap allocation, producing the heap-buffer-overflow read.
